title: Derived coefficient extension under profinite slice restriction
statement: Let Lambda be a commutative condensed ring and S any profinite set. Let R=Lambda(*), K the actual profinite slice topology, O=Lambda restricted to the slice, A its terminal section ring. Define d:constant_K R -> O as constant(profiniteScalarMap R->A) followed by the terminal constant-section counit. For every unbounded complex of module sheaves over constant R on the profinite point, coefficient extension to Lambda followed by internal-module transport and slice mapMod is naturally isomorphic to commutativeConstantSliceRestriction [lem-zl-commutative-constant-slice-restriction] followed by the universal derived coefficient extension along d and the slice internal-module equivalence. This is a comparison before applying constant realization of ordinary R-modules; it asserts no scalar extension to A.

proof.text: Apply profinite_coefficient_slice_ordinary to the two actual fixed models and the definitional direct scalar map, obtaining an ordinary natural isomorphism tau.

Exact localized-site restriction preserves K-flat complexes. Transport its output along constantSheafOverIso. Scalar restriction along a ring-sheaf isomorphism preserves K-flatness: its restricted regular module is isomorphic to the source regular module, hence flat, so apply flat scalar restriction. The regular-module isomorphism is constructed sectionwise from the inverse ring isomorphism; flatness is transported using the explicit site-tensor to monoidal-tensor comparison. This proves K-flat preservation for commutativeConstantSliceRestriction.

Postcompose the original cochain counit with exact internal-module transport and actual slice mapMod. Precompose the slice counit with exact constant-slice restriction and postcompose with the exact slice equivalence; use tau to identify the two ordinary targets. Descend these transformations through the full and essentially surjective homotopy quotient. On every flat-term K-flat resolving object both are isomorphisms, by the fixed models computes fields and step 2. Site-derived-tensor descent presents the entire derived category as the localization of this resolving full subcategory. Fully faithful whiskering along that localization lifts the ratio of the two isomorphisms uniquely to a natural isomorphism on the entire derived category. Finally apply mapDerivedCategoryCompIso to express the left functor in exactly the stated form.

proof_origin.note: Lean proof of the unbounded derived lift from the ordinary slice comparison. Uses the existing localization of flat-term K-flat objects and existing slice K-flat theorem; no general ringed-topos pullback theorem or new resolving existence assertion.
